rationale: The hypothesis that ACBD6-associated neurodevelopmental disorder (OMIM #620785) is predominantly characterized by early developmental delay transitioning into a mixed hypokinetic-hyperkinetic movement disorder (dystonia and parkinsonism/choreoathetosis) is strongly supported by the largest international cohort (Kaiyrzhanov et al., 2024; n=45), where dystonia occurs in 94% and parkinsonism emerges in 32%. However, the hypothesis is conflicted in two critical aspects: first, parkinsonism is not present in most affected individuals (only 32%), and chorea is secondary to dystonia and tremor, limiting its sensitivity as a defining feature; second, the claim that the disorder presents strictly without metabolic/systemic decompensation is directly contradicted by Yeetong et al. (2022), who described biallelic ACBD6-mutated patients presenting with cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, pancytopenia, and renal failure leading to early mortality. Furthermore, discriminating ACBD6 from GNAO1, NKX2-1, and NBIA relies heavily on key neuroimaging hallmarks (e.g., hypertrophy of the clava in 24%, anterior commissure hypoplasia in 66%, corpus callosum anomalies in 70%) rather than clinical phenomenology alone.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 45 affected individuals from 28 families with bi-allelic ACBD6 variants, 100% presented with global developmental delay/intellectual disability and 97% had movement disorders. Dystonia was the most common movement disorder (94%), accompanied by gait impairment (94%), cerebellar ataxia (85%), jerky upper limb tremor (63%), head tremor (59%), and parkinsonism/hypokinesia developing with advancing age in 32%. Midline neuroimaging anomalies were prominent, including corpus callosum abnormalities (70%), hypoplasia/agenesis of the anterior commissure (66%), and hypertrophy of the clava (24%).

source.title: Bi-allelic ACBD6 variants lead to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with progressive and complex movement disorders
source.quote: The affected individuals (23 males and 22 females), aged 1-50 years, typically present with a complex and progressive disease involving moderate-to-severe global developmental delay/intellectual disability (100%) with significant expressive language impairment (98%), movement disorders (97%), facial dysmorphism (95%) and mild cerebellar ataxia (85%) associated with gait impairment (94%), limb spasticity/hypertonia (76%), oculomotor (71%) and behavioural abnormalities (65%), overweight (59%), microcephaly (39%) and epilepsy (33%). The most conspicuous and common movement disorder was dystonia (94%), frequently leading to early-onset progressive postural deformities (97%), limb dystonia (55%) and cervical dystonia (31%). A jerky tremor in the upper limbs (63%), a mild head tremor (59%), parkinsonism/hypokinesia developing with advancing age (32%) and simple motor and vocal tics were among other frequent movement disorders.

evidence.text: A phenotypic expansion of ACBD6 deficiency reported two siblings with homozygous truncating variants who exhibited severe systemic and metabolic pathology, specifically morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure leading to death in their early 30s, showing that ACBD6 mutations can cause fatal multisystem visceral disease rather than an isolated neurodevelopmental movement disorder.

source.title: Neurodevelopmental Disorder, Obesity, Pancytopenia, Diabetes Mellitus, Cirrhosis, and Renal Failure in ACBD6-Associated Syndrome: A Case Report
source.quote: Clinical manifestations that have never been previously reported include morbid obesity, pancytopenia with severe infections, diabetes mellitus, cirrhosis, and renal failure, leading to deaths in their early 30s. Molecular studies identified a novel homozygous 1 base-pair duplication (c.360dup; p.Leu121Thrfs*27) in the ACBD6 gene.

evidence.text: Systematic cluster analysis of childhood-onset hyperkinetic movement disorders across 210 monogenic conditions highlights that dystonia, chorea, and dyskinesia heavily overlap between neurodevelopmental delay and developmental epileptic encephalopathy clusters. Recessive ACBD6 is noted in hyperkinetic neurodevelopmental syndromic groupings where axial dystonia is a prominent presentation, but dystonia alone does not differentiate it cleanly without genetic or structural markers.

source.quote: Across both groups, dystonia was the most frequently reported movement disorder, followed in order by chorea, ataxia, dyskinesia, and myoclonus... suggest recessive ACBD6 mutations, where axial dystonia is...

evidence.text: ACBD6 has been recently recognized as a monogenic cause of genetic chorea and hyperkinetic movement abnormalities linked to cerebral palsy mimics and neurodevelopmental disorders, but shares significant phenomenological overlap with other novel and established hyperkinetic conditions.

source.quote: Several novel genetic conditions have been linked to chorea over the last 3 years, including mutations in FTH1, NAA60, ACBD6 or TOR1AIP2... Recently, a bi-allelic loss-of-function mutation in the ACBD6... typically linked to neurodevelopmental disorder (cerebral palsy...)

conflicts: The hypothesis asserts the absence of metabolic decompensation or systemic disease, whereas Yeetong et al. (2022) documented homozygous ACBD6 loss-of-function variants resulting in cirrhosis, diabetes mellitus, and end-stage renal failure.

The hypothesis emphasizes parkinsonism as a primary discriminating feature, but Kaiyrzhanov et al. (2024) found parkinsonism/hypokinesia in only 32% (14/45) of patients, demonstrating that its absence cannot rule out the condition.

new_directions.question_text: What genetic or molecular modifiers determine whether ACBD6 biallelic loss-of-function leads to isolated neurodevelopmental movement disorders versus severe visceral involvement (hepatic cirrhosis, pancytopenia, renal failure)?
new_directions.rationale: Resolving the phenotypic dichotomy between the Kaiyrzhanov et al. neurodevelopmental cohort and the Yeetong et al. multiorgan failure cohort is critical for accurate clinical prognosis and surveillance.

new_directions.question_text: Can the combination of clava hypertrophy and anterior commissure agenesis/hypoplasia on brain MRI serve as a definitive radiologic biomarker to distinguish ACBD6 disorder from GNAO1 and NBIA?
new_directions.rationale: Phenotypic overlap among hyperkinetic childhood disorders makes clinical separation challenging; quantitative MRI validation of clava hypertrophy could allow precise differentiation without whole-exome sequencing delay.
